summary: Round 1 (exhaustive) of N06-design-ux at e1965ab: 4 major, 8 minor, 3 info. SDD line citations L254, L299-L302, L344, L347, L376, L436-L437 still hold; the Q39(a) catalogue (L148-L164) is identical to 161def0; D2 singular and plural sentences match sdd section 8 exactly; N = 0 opens no dialog; Q36, Q44, Q46-Q48, Q53, Q54 and DD-1/DD-2 are as frozen; upstream lists the three contracts; section 11 removals all map to answered questions. Majors: an undefined failure state for the D2 pre-dialog re-fetch (NFR-006 AC-1), and three unmarked additions with no requirement (Show password, Show all to-dos, Signed in as). Sign-up wording mismatch with sdd L155/L209 judged minor: sdd section 6.1 and section 8 give exact copy to the UX design, Q39(a) approved Account created. Log in., and the SDD quote predates that approval.

findings.message: The Clear all completed click re-fetches the list before D2 opens, but the design defines no state for a failure of that re-fetch (network, 5xx, other non-401). Section 7.3 maps clear-completed only to inside D2, which is not open yet, and no page-level alert, copy, next step or focus target is given for this path. NFR-006 AC-1 requires a message with a next step for any failed operation, and sdd section 6.1 leaves which surface each state uses to the UX design.
findings.suggestion: Add a D2 opening-sequence failure row: no dialog opens, the button leaves its busy state, a page-level alert above the list (e.g. the clear-completed or load-list try-again message, named explicitly) with its next step, and focus stays on Clear all completed; add the row to section 7.3 (L508) and section 6. Keep L299-L302 on their current lines because sdd section 8 cites them.

findings.message: A Show password checkbox on S1 and S2 is a behaviour no requirement, AC or clarification states, and it is not marked [proposed]. Its only stated reason is WCAG 3.3.8, a 2.2 criterion that section 9.2 itself says is not part of the NFR-001 audit level (Q44: 2.1 AA). L22 claims the design adds no behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Remove the Show password control from S1, S2 and the component inventory, or mark it [proposed] with a reason and list it in section 11 as a question for the requester before build.

findings.message: The No matching to-dos state adds a Show all to-dos link that clears status, q and page. REQ-LIST-001 AC-4 and REQ-LIST-002 AC-4 require only the state; the link is new navigation behaviour with no requirement and no [proposed] mark (sdd section 12.1 item 8 records a Show all to-dos next step as a rejected option, and Q48 declined a filter-clearing link on the list screen in another case).
findings.suggestion: Drop the link (the filter and search controls stay on screen, and the copy already says try a different search or filter), or mark it [proposed] and list it in section 11 for the requester.

findings.message: The signed-in header shows Signed in as {identifier}. No requirement or SDD section asks the UI to display the identifier; it is an unmarked addition (the contract returning Session.user.identifier does not by itself make it a UI requirement).
findings.suggestion: Remove the identifier text from the header (keep the app name and Log out), or mark it [proposed] with a reason and list it in section 11 for the requester.

findings.message: The sign-up success message is Account created. Log in. in the design, but sdd.md L155 and L209 quote Account created — log in. The design text is the one approved in Q39(a) (already present at 161def0 L209) and sdd section 6.1 L382-L384 and section 8 give exact copy to the UX design; the SDD quote predates Q39 (b36e7df). Testers reading the SDD could assert the wrong string, and the design does not record the discrepancy.
findings.suggestion: Keep the design wording; add a note in section 11 that the Q39(a) text governs and that sdd L155/L209 should be aligned at the next re-freeze; the orchestrator raises it.

findings.message: Section 9.1 claims a WCAG 2.1 Level AA review but omits several 2.1 A/AA criteria: 1.3.3 Sensory characteristics, 1.4.5 Images of text, 2.4.5 Multiple ways, 3.1.2 Language of parts, and the N/A rows 1.2.x and 1.4.2.
findings.suggestion: Add the missing rows with their disposition (2.4.5 in particular needs a stated basis, e.g. list links plus search).

findings.message: The S3 Loading row says the loading text is shown in place of the list for first load or any re-query, and in the same cell that on re-query the existing rows stay; it also says previous rows are removed during first load, when there are none. The two cases read as contradictory.
findings.suggestion: Within the same line (sdd cites L254): first load shows the loading text in place of the list; a re-query keeps the rows with aria-busy and shows no replacement text.

findings.message: Section 3 says each route moves focus to the h1 on navigation, and section 6 says Route change; a filter, search or page change is also a router navigation, so read literally this conflicts with L436. sdd section 9 L560 states the rule as a route (pathname) change.
findings.suggestion: Say on a pathname change (not on a query-string-only change), matching sdd section 9.

findings.message: Section 6 gives no focus target for paths whose invoking control disappears or whose dialog closes on an error: the S3 404 on toggle then refresh, D1 404 opened from S3, D1 404 on S5, and toggle failure. sdd section 9 gives a fallback rule, but the design table that the build follows is silent.
findings.suggestion: Add rows: focus to the h1 (or the alert) after a 404 refresh and after D1 closes on a 404; stays on the checkbox after a toggle failure.

findings.message: L23 says section 11 records the design decisions, but the remaining [proposed] items (D2 heading L304, singular live-region text L316, focus after D2 not opened L444, all S7 copy and motion L467-L468, E1 copy L493, section 7.3 copy L497) are not collected there; the approver cannot see what still awaits confirmation versus what sdd sections 6.1 and 8 already delegate to the design.
findings.suggestion: List every [proposed] item in section 11 with its reason and whether it needs a requester decision or is design-owned under sdd section 6.1 L382-L384 or section 8 L501.

findings.message: Copy that stood in section 4 when Q39(a) and Q42 approved it was reworded without a recorded reason: Could not update that to-do. Try again.; Your to-dos could not be loaded.; The to-do could not be deleted. Try again.; Completed to-dos could not be deleted. Try again.; the D2 heading Delete all completed to-dos?; and the generic Something went wrong. Please try again. The changes follow NFR-006 and sdd section 6.1 (name the failed action and a next step), but S3/D1/D2 tables show them without the [proposed] mark that section 7.3 L497 applies.
findings.suggestion: Record in section 11 each approved string that changed, its new text and the reason (NFR-006 / sdd section 6.1), and mark them consistently.

findings.message: The S6 state table has no load-error state (getTodo fails with a non-401, non-404), while S5 has one at L377; only the generic load-todo row of section 7.3 covers it.
findings.suggestion: Add an S6 load-error row: This to-do could not be loaded. Please try again. with Retry, in place of the form.

findings.message: The log-out failure message is defined but not whether the user stays signed in and on the same screen after it (sdd section 4.1 is also silent).
findings.suggestion: State that the session state and screen are unchanged and focus moves to the alert.

findings.message: Two hand-computed contrast figures look slightly off: text.danger on surface.danger computes to about 5.9:1 (stated 6.0:1) and focus.ring on surface.danger to about 6.1:1 (stated 5.9:1). Both stay above their thresholds, and section 9 already asks web-qa to verify by tool.
findings.suggestion: Correct the figures when web-qa verifies them.

findings.message: D2 success can return deletedCount 0 (cleared in another tab after the dialog opened); the live-region text then reads Deleted 0 completed to-dos. No requirement covers it.
findings.suggestion: Optionally note the 0 case wording, or accept the plural as written.
